History:
- Main complaint: 7 days of fever with alternating hot/cold episodes and night sweats.
- Course: Persistent despite OTC antipyretics; partial, temporary relief.
- Associated symptoms: Diffuse myalgias, nausea, poor appetite, reduced fluid intake, fatigue. No cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, new/worsening headache, rash, joint swelling, dysuria, or urinary frequency.
- Travel history: Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago; multi-week trip with rural trekking/cycling through farmland and visits to cities. Took malaria chemoprophylaxis (daily; specific agent not recalled; patient believes an additional tablet was taken with the first).
- Functional impact: Difficulty working due to fatigue.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic back pain related to prolonged sitting/poor posture; under physiotherapy.
- History of headaches/migraines related to screen use and weather.
- Family history: Father died of myocardial infarction at 68.
- Allergies: Seasonal/pollen (hay fever). No medication allergies reported.
- Medications: 
  - Seroxat (paroxetine) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Ibuprofen — over-the-counter use; dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Paracetamol — over-the-counter use; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social: Nurse; up to date on vaccinations including Hepatitis B. Non-smoker. Moderate alcohol. Regular moderate exercise.

Physical Examination:
- Not recorded. (Teleconsultation; in-person exam planned.)
- Reported negatives: No neck stiffness, no rash, no swollen joints.

Impression:
- Undifferentiated febrile illness for 1 week in a recent traveler from Vietnam with night sweats, myalgias, and nausea, without localizing respiratory or urinary symptoms; concern for travel-related infection.
- DDx (consistent with transcript):
  - Malaria: Travel to Vietnam with rural exposure; paroxysmal fevers/chills/sweats and myalgias; prophylaxis not fully protective.
  - Enteric fever (typhoid/paratyphoid): Prolonged fever post–SE Asia travel with few focal findings.
  - Common viral syndrome: Systemic symptoms without focal source; occupational exposure as a nurse.

Management Plan:
- In-person evaluation today at central clinic (preferred) or local A&E if more convenient.
- Planned investigations (post-exam):
  - Malaria testing: Thick and thin blood films.
  - “Inflammatory markers and general blood tests” per treating clinician (e.g., CBC, CRP/ESR; specifics to be determined by examining clinician).
- Administrative: Clinician to message admin team to book visit; patient to call the provided number to be scheduled; note to be available for reception if attending A&E.
- Work status: Advised not to work until evaluation completed and cause identified.

Patient Summary:
- 32-year-old with one week of persistent fever, chills, night sweats, myalgias, and nausea after travel to rural/urban Vietnam 4 weeks ago. No clear localizing source. High suspicion for malaria or other travel-related infection. Urgent in-person assessment and malaria testing arranged.

Key Takeaways:
- Seek in-person evaluation today for exam and urgent labs including malaria films.
- Do not attend work until the cause of fever is identified and managed.

Next Steps:
- Attend scheduled clinic or A&E today; bring/mention these notes.
- Proceed with malaria thick/thin films and initial blood tests as directed after exam.
- Further management will depend on exam and test results; urgency to be determined by examining clinician.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: No vital signs; no physical examination findings; pregnancy status/LMP not recorded; full medication list with doses/frequencies not documented; detailed travel exposures (freshwater immersion, insect bite frequency, animal exposures, sexual exposures, food/water hygiene, specific travel vaccinations) not recorded; COVID/respiratory testing status not recorded.
- Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear with minor hesitations and brief incomplete lines; clinically adequate.
